1.o: In this chapter we have, I. A command given to Jonah to preach at Nineveh, ver. 1, 2. II. Jonah's disobedience to that command, ver. 3. III. The pursuit and arrest of him for that disobedience by a storm, in which he was asleep, ver. 4-6. IV. The discovery of him, and his disobedience, to be the cause of the storm, ver. 7-10. V. The casting of him into the sea, for the stilling of the storm, ver. 11-16. VI. The miraculous preservation of his life there in the belly of a fish (ver.
1.i: God sends Jonah to Nineveh, but Jonah flees by ship, and a great storm and a great fish stop him.
1.p: Lord, You chase after us when we run. Help us to listen the first time. Amen.
1.l: If you have been running from something God asked you to do, tell Him you are ready to turn around.
q: Jonah ran from God and still God went after him. What does that tell you about God?

2.o: We left Jonah in the belly of the fish, and had reason to think we should hear no more of him, that if he were not destroyed by the waters of the sea he would be consumed in the bowels of that leviathan, "out of whose mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire, and whose breath kindles coals," Job xli. 19, 21. But God brings his people through fire, and through water (Ps. lxvi. 12); and by his power, behold, Jonah the prophet is yet alive, and is heard of again.
2.i: From inside the great fish, Jonah prays a prayer of thanks, and God has the fish release him onto dry land.
2.p: Lord, You hear us even from the deepest places. Thank You for saving us. Amen.
2.l: Say a thank-you prayer today for a time God rescued you, even from something small.
q: Jonah prayed from the worst place. Where do you need to pray from right now?

3.o: In this chapter we have, I. Jonah's mission renewed, and the command a second time given him to go preach at Nineveh, ver. 1, 2. II. Jonah's message to Nineveh faithfully delivered, by which its speedy overthrow was threatened, ver. 3, 4. III. The repentance, humiliation, and reformation of the Ninevites hereupon, ver. 5-9. IV. God's gracious revocation of the sentence passed upon them, and the preventing of the ruin threatened, ver. 10.
3.i: Jonah finally preaches in Nineveh, and the whole city repents, from the king to the animals.
3.p: Lord, You are merciful. Help us to turn from what is wrong, and to speak up when You send us. Amen.
3.l: If you need to say sorry to someone, go and do it today.
q: A whole city turned back to God after one short message. What might happen if you were that bold?

4.o: We read, with a great deal of pleasure, in the close of the foregoing chapter, concerning the repentance of Nineveh; but in this chapter we read, with a great deal of uneasiness, concerning the sin of Jonah; and, as there is joy in heaven and earth for the conversion of sinners, so there is grief for the follies and infirmities of saints. In all the book of God we scarcely find a "servant of the Lord"
4.i: Jonah sulks outside Nineveh, and God uses a plant and a worm to ask whether He should care for the great city.
4.p: Lord, You are gracious and compassionate. Give us hearts like Yours for every person. Amen.
4.l: Think of someone you find hard to like, and ask God to help you care about them.
q: God cared about people Jonah did not. Who do you find it hard to care about?
